name: Congenital Bilateral Elbow Dislocation

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Congenital Elbow Dislocation

criteria.description: Presence of visible deformity and limited range of motion in both elbows at birth
Radiographic evidence of posterior or anterior dislocation of the elbow joint bilaterally
No history of traumatic injury causing elbow dislocation
Presence of associated musculoskeletal anomalies such as hypoplastic or malformed distal humerus or ulna

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Bilateral clinical deformity and radiographic confirmation of elbow dislocation at birth without trauma history
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by imaging; genetic testing may be considered if syndromic features are present.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Bilateral elbow joint dislocation present at birth
searchTerms: bilateral elbow joint displacement from birth

pathognomonic.symptomName: Restricted elbow flexion and extension bilaterally
searchTerms: limited bending and straightening of elbows

common.symptomName: Visible deformity with posterior prominence of the elbow
searchTerms: visible elbow deformity with back prominence
elbow bone sticks out at back
prominent bump on back of elbow

common.symptomName: Mild to moderate limitation of forearm supination and pronation
searchTerms: difficulty rotating forearm palm up or down

common.symptomName: Muscle hypoplasia around the elbow joint

searchTerms: arm bent away from body at elbow

occasional.symptomName: Mild pain or discomfort during elbow movement
Delayed motor milestones related to upper limb function
searchTerms: slow development of upper limb skills

occasional.symptomName: Mild swelling around the elbow joint

rare.symptomName: Ulnar nerve neuropathy symptoms such as numbness or tingling
searchTerms: numbness or tingling in ulnar nerve area
tingling in ring and little fingers

rare.symptomName: Associated congenital anomalies such as syndactyly or clinodactyly
Elbow joint instability leading to recurrent subluxations
searchTerms: unstable elbow causing repeated partial dislocations

imaging: X-ray showing posterior or anterior dislocation of the elbow joint bilaterally
Ultrasound or MRI may show soft tissue abnormalities around the elbow
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified; may be associated with syndromic conditions in rare cases
other: Physical examination revealing fixed deformity and limited range of motion

distinguishingFeatures: Absence of congenital deformity at birth
Often associated with muscle fibrosis and weakness
Not primarily characterized by joint dislocation

redFlags: Severe neurovascular compromise of the upper limb
Signs of ulnar nerve entrapment or neuropathy
references: Journal of Pediatric Orthopedics, 2018; Bilateral Congenital Elbow Dislocation Case Studies
